chunks: Al-Shaykh al-Faqih Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq narrated to us. He said: Abdul Aziz b. Yahya al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Al-Mughira b. Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Jabir b. Salama narrated to me. He said: Husayn b. Hasan narrated to us from Amir al-Siraj from Salam al-Khath'ami from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon him.

He said: Whoever fasts one day in Rajab, from its beginning or its middle or its end, Allah will make Paradise obligatory for him. He will bring him to us, in our rank, on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever fasts two days in Rajab, it will be said to him: Resume your work, for everything that has passed has been forgiven. Whoever fasts three days in Rajab, it will be said to him: Everything that has passed and everything that will remain has been forgiven, so intercede for whichever sinner you wish from your brethren and acquaintances. Whoever fasts seven days in Rajab, the seven doors of Hell will be locked from him. Whoever fasts eight days in Rajab, the eight doors of Paradise will be opened for him, and he will enter whichever one he wishes.

key_terms.صوم رجب: fasting in the month of Rajab

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for fasting in the month of Rajab?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir describes the escalating spiritual rewards for fasting in the sacred month of Rajab. One day of fasting earns Paradise and the rank of the Ahl al-Bayt on the Day of Resurrection. Two days bring forgiveness of all past sins. Three days bring forgiveness of past and future sins, plus the ability to intercede for sinful brethren. Seven days close the seven gates of Hell. Eight days open the eight gates of Paradise, with entry through any gate of one's choosing. This hadith was part of the Amali lecture given in a 367 AH Rajab gathering, making the topic especially timely for the audience.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Shaykh Al-Faqih Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq narrated to us. He said: `Abdul `Aziz b. Yahya al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Al-Mughira b. Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Jabir b. Salama narrated to us. He said: Husayn b. Hasan narrated to us from `Amer al-Sarraj from Salam al-Khath`ami from Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir (as).

He said: "Whomever fasts one day in Rajab, from its beginning or its middle or its end, Allah will make Paradise obligatory for him. He will bring him to us, in our rank, on the Day of Resurrection. Whomever fasts two days in Rajab, it will be said to him: “Resume your work, for everything that has passed has been forgiven.” Whomever fasts three days in Rajab, it will be said to him: “Everything that has passed and everything that will remain has been forgiven, so intercede for whichever sinner you wish from your brethren to your acquaintances.” Whomever fasts seven days in Rajab, the seven doors of Hell will be locked from him. Whomever fasts eight days in Rajab, the eight doors of Paradise will be opened for him, and he will be able to enter whichever one he wants."
